story_1: We built Three Acts after the same brief showed up for the fourth time: a marketing site, somewhere non-technical for an editor to make changes, and no budget to rebuild the plumbing from scratch each time. Three Acts is that shape, built once and left open to configure rather than rewrite.

The public site renders to static HTML by default. React only ships where a page actually needs it — cart, checkout, sign-in, a form — as an isolated island, not a framework wrapped around every route.

Every collection, field and constraint is declared once in the collection registry. The editor, the API's validation and the generated Postgres schema all read the same file, so the three never drift apart.

Neither the public site nor the editorial app ever holds a database credential or a payment key. Every write and every auth call goes through the API app — the one place secrets live, and the one place to audit.
A client fork edits the registry, the seed data, the shop config and the theme tokens — not the plumbing underneath. Swap the backend, keep the site.

value_tiles_2.title: Static-first
value_tiles_2.description: Every route pre-renders to HTML; islands hydrate only what needs to be interactive.

value_tiles_2.title: One registry
value_tiles_2.description: Collections, fields and constraints declared once, shared by the editor, the API and the schema.

value_tiles_2.title: Swap the backend
value_tiles_2.description: File-backed storage today, Postgres or Supabase tomorrow — the same interface either way.

value_tiles_2.title: Everything through the API
value_tiles_2.description: Every browser write and every auth call goes through one app. No app holds a provider credential.

value_tiles_2.title: Fork in an afternoon
value_tiles_2.description: Rename the brand, edit the registry, swap the seed data — the plumbing stays put.

value_tiles_2.title: Wireframe design system
value_tiles_2.description: Black, white and one gray. Hierarchy comes from size and space, not colour.

process_steps_3.title: Fork
process_steps_3.description: Clone the repo, then rename the brand in site.ts and the design tokens in theme.css.

process_steps_3.title: Configure the registry
process_steps_3.description: Add, remove or retype collections and fields in the collection registry for the client's real content and product model.

process_steps_3.title: Seed and design
process_steps_3.description: Replace the example seed data, swap in the client's real copy and imagery, and adjust the theme tokens to the client's brand.

process_steps_3.title: Connect a store
process_steps_3.description: Point the data and storage backends at Postgres or Supabase — or keep the zero-configuration file-backed store for a lightweight site with no shop.

process_steps_3.title: Deploy
process_steps_3.description: Set the client's own secrets, deploy the web, CMS and API apps, and run the first publish.

about.title_5: One template, three apps, no re-plumbing
about.lede_6: Three Acts is a static-first Astro site, a private CMS and a typed API bridge, versioned together in one repo. Here's why we built it that way, and what forking it actually looks like.
